newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Earthquake rocks Pakistan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks Pakistan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan.

text.p: An earthquake rocked north and central Pakistan, Afghanistan and Tajikistan on Tuesday, killing a 60-year-old Pakistani, witnesses said.

An official at Pakistan's Meteorology Department in the north-western city of Peshawar said the centre of the quake, which measured 6.5 on the open-ended Richter scale, was about 250 km (150 miles) north of the city in the Hindu Kush mountain range.
Residents in the Pakistan town of Muridke, north of Lahore, said a 60-year-old man was killed there when a house collapsed.
The quake, also jolted the capital Islamabad and the nearby city of Rawalpindi, residents said.
It was felt in the Indian capital New Delhi 1,000 km (600 miles) away, but seismologists there said there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
One person was reported injured by a falling brick in Kabul in neighbouring Afghanistan.
A tremor was reported in Tajikistan as measuring between five and seven points on the 12-point Russian scale.
No casualties were initially reported, there, but telephone lines from the capital Dushanbe to the worst affected areas were out of order.
Tajikistan seismologists said the centre was on the border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan, some 260 km (150 miles) south-east of Dushanbe.
Shockwaves of smaller strength spread throughout Tajikistan and into neighbouring Uzbekistan, the scientists said.
An earthquake killed 1,560 people in eastern Iran on Saturday, according to a revised casualty toll given by a senior Iranian Interior Ministry official.
A second jolt which hit Iran late on Monday, was not reported to have caused any casualties.
